before.title: Adopted continuum matter models and their evolution equations
before.statement: Adopt, on top of the flat spacetime postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], the SI conventions [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and the particle premises [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], the following classical continuum matter models on an open set $\Omega\subseteq A$: (i) Scalar field. A real smooth dimensionless field $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, a smooth potential $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with values in inverse square metres and a constant $K>0$ in joule per metre have the field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ -- the Euler-Lagrange equation of the adopted action on compactly supported variations ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]); the model's stress-energy tensor is the Hilbert tensor of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]. (ii) Dust. A $C^1$ rest energy density $\rho>0$ (joule per cubic metre) and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ ($\eta(n,n)=-1$) satisfy $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; the stress-energy tensor is $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$. (iii) Perfect fluid. $C^1$ fields $\varepsilon$ (energy density) and $P$ (pressure), both in joule per cubic metre, and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ satisfy the energy-balance and Euler equations of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; an equation of state or evolution equation determining $P$ is part of the model and is not supplied by this postulate; the stress-energy tensor is $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$. (iv) Additivity. The total stress-energy tensor of a composite system is the sum of the stress-energy tensors of its constituents (tensor-field addition on $\Omega$). This postulate adopts model equations and tensor identifications only: it does not assert conservation of the tensors (that is derived from these equations in [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]), does not select any force law, interaction, equation of state, thermodynamic or dissipative behaviour, does not claim that these models exhaust physical matter, and contains no empirical premise, measurement or uncertainty statement.
before.strategy: Adopted physical premise; no proof obligation (the schema records postulates with formulation, scope and sources, not a deduction). The mathematical content used in the formulation is confined to the model equations and the displayed tensors; conservation is deliberately NOT part of this postulate. Sources: the scalar action and equation of motion are 4.5.1 of Tong; the fluid equations are 4.5.4 of Tong and the displayed tensors are (4.53) of Tong, (1.106)-(1.110) of Carroll and 9.2.3-9.2.6 of Crowell; the choice to adopt, rather than derive, the matter dynamics follows the source statements that conservation follows from each model's own equations of motion (Carroll p. 30) and that matter actions and equations of state are separate model assumptions (Tong 4.5). No empirical support is claimed.

after.title: Adopted continuum matter models and their evolution equations
after.statement: Adopt, on top of the flat spacetime postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], the SI conventions [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and the particle premises [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], the following classical continuum matter models on an open set $\Omega\subseteq A$: (i) Scalar field. A real smooth dimensionless field $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, a smooth potential $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with values in inverse square metres and a constant $K>0$ in joule per metre have the field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ -- the Euler-Lagrange equation of the adopted local action density, with stationarity defined by the finite relative action for compactly supported field variations ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]); the model's stress-energy tensor is the Hilbert tensor of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]. (ii) Dust. A $C^1$ rest energy density $\rho>0$ (joule per cubic metre) and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ ($\eta(n,n)=-1$) satisfy $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; the stress-energy tensor is $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$. (iii) Perfect fluid. $C^1$ fields $\varepsilon$ (energy density) and $P$ (pressure), both in joule per cubic metre, and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ satisfy the energy-balance and Euler equations of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; an equation of state or evolution equation determining $P$ is part of the model and is not supplied by this postulate; the stress-energy tensor is $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$. (iv) Additivity. The total stress-energy tensor of a composite system is the sum of the stress-energy tensors of its constituents (tensor-field addition on $\Omega$). (v) Adopted observer readings and units. For a tensor physically assigned to matter in this model, all inertial components $T^{ab}$ have units joule per cubic metre. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, an ideal observer with future unit direction $n$ and four-velocity $U=cn$ reads the numerical contractions of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] as energy density $\varepsilon_n=T^{ab}n_an_b$, momentum density $\pi_n^a=-c^{-1}h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$ and rest stress $S_n^{ab}=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd}$. Here $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$. In an adapted inertial frame these are $T^{00}$, $T^{0i}/c$ and $T^{ij}$ respectively, and the energy-flux components are $cT^{i0}=c^2\pi_n^i$. Momentum density has units kilogram per square metre per second; energy flux has units watt per square metre; rest stress has units joule per cubic metre. These identifications are adopted model readings, not mathematical facts about an arbitrary symmetric tensor and not reported measurements. If $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ is assigned to external exchange, the spatial components $f^i$ are force per volume and $cf^0$ is power per volume: the corresponding numerical balances are $\partial_t(T^{00})+\partial_i(cT^{i0})=cf^0$ and $\partial_t(T^{0j}/c)+\partial_iT^{ij}=f^j$. Neither assignment selects a force law or asserts conservation. This postulate adopts model equations and tensor identifications only: it does not assert conservation of the tensors (that is derived from these equations in [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]), does not select any force law, interaction, equation of state, thermodynamic or dissipative behaviour, does not claim that these models exhaust physical matter, and contains no empirical premise, measurement or uncertainty statement.

Sources: the scalar action and equation of motion are 4.5.1 of Tong; the fluid equations are 4.5.4 of Tong and the displayed tensors are (4.53) of Tong, (1.106)-(1.110) of Carroll and 9.2.3-9.2.6 of Crowell; the choice to adopt, rather than derive, the matter dynamics follows the source statements that conservation follows from each model's own equations of motion (Carroll p. 30) and that matter actions and equations of state are separate model assumptions (Tong 4.5). No empirical support is claimed. The observer component reading removed from mathematical definitions/lemmas is explicitly adopted in(v), including the exact c factors: $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$ turns the tensor balance into the two displayed SI balances, while the observer-decomposition lemma provides only the numerical contractions/components. This is preservation of the framework's stated interpretation, not a new empirical law or a deduction of an observer measurement. Local relative actions, not a possibly divergent background integral over all Omega, formulate(i).

before.title: Local conservation of stress-energy for the adopted matter models
before.statement: Under the matter premises of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]]: (a) If $\varphi$ is a smooth scalar field solving the adopted field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$, then the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]) satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$, in every inertial chart. (b) If $\rho>0$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted dust equations, then $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely if $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ and $\rho>0$ then the dust equations hold. (c) If $\varepsilon,P$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted fluid equations, then $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely conservation of that $T$ implies the two fluid equations. (d) For a $C^1$ symmetric tensor field prescribed on $\Omega$ that is not obtained from one of the adopted models together with its field equations, no conservation is asserted; a conservation statement about such a field is an additional explicit premise. (e) The theorem is a conditional deduction from the adopted model equations; it asserts no interaction, force law, cross section, measurement or empirical fact, and its conclusions inherit the scope of the postulate.
before.strategy: Clause (a) is [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]] evaluated on the solutions of the adopted field equation; clause (b) is [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]; clause (c) is [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]. Clause (d) records the absence of any derivation for arbitrary prescribed tensors: the local balance $\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$ of [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]] is a definition, and no hypothesis in this page forces $f=0$ for an arbitrary $T$. Clause (e) restates the physical scope. No empirical premise is used and the conclusion carries no measurement interpretation.

after.title: Local conservation of stress-energy for the adopted matter models
after.statement:
Under the matter premises of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]]: (a) If $\varphi$ is a smooth scalar field solving the adopted field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$, then the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]) satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$, in every inertial chart. (b) If $ho>0$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted dust equations, then $T=ho\,n\otimes n$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely if $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ and $ho>0$ then the dust equations hold. (c) If $\varepsilon,P$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted fluid equations, then $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely conservation of that $T$ implies the two fluid equations. (d) For a $C^1$ symmetric tensor field prescribed on $\Omega$ that is not obtained from one of the adopted models together with its field equations, no conservation is asserted; a conservation statement about such a field is an additional explicit premise. (e) The theorem is a conditional deduction from the adopted model equations; it asserts no interaction, force law, cross section, measurement or empirical fact, and its conclusions inherit the scope of the postulate. Under the already stated homogeneous dust reading, the tensor boost computation has the conditional physical interpretation $T'^{00}=\gamma^2ho$. For comoving identical massive particles with fixed rest mass $m$, rest number density $
u$ and $ho=
u mc^2$, a rest rectangular parcel has boosted simultaneous volume $1/\gamma$ times its rest volume (the parallel length contracts and transverse lengths are unchanged), so its particle density is $\gamma
u$; the adopted massive-particle reading gives each particle energy $\gamma mc^2$. Thus the two factors in $\gamma^2ho$ correspond respectively to particle energy and volume/density. This is conditional model interpretation for that homogeneous particle realization, not a derivation of the continuum from microscopic dynamics, a claim about arbitrary tensors, or empirical evidence.
after.strategy: Clause (a) is [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]] evaluated on the solutions of the adopted field equation; clause (b) is [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]; clause (c) is [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]. Clause (d) records the absence of any derivation for arbitrary prescribed tensors: the local balance $\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$ of [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]] is a definition, and no hypothesis in this page forces $f=0$ for an arbitrary $T$. Clause (e) restates the physical scope. No empirical premise is used and the conclusions inherit only the adopted ideal model readings, with no reported measurement or empirical support. For the preserved dust energy/volume explanation, use the massive-particle energy formula of [[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]] and the parallel/transverse length formulas of [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]] on the stipulated homogeneous rest rectangular parcel. Divide its same particle count by the contracted simultaneous volume and multiply by the particle energy. The exact tensor computation itself is $T'^{00}=\rho(\Lambda^0{}_0)^2=\gamma^2\rho$ from [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]](iii). This physical explanation is restricted to the explicitly interpreted homogeneous dust and introduces no interaction, statistical or measured claim.

before.title: Integrated four-momentum of an isolated system on finite slices
before.statement: Let $x$ be an inertial chart, let $\bar K$ be a closed spatial box and $s_1<s_2$, and let $T$ be the total stress-energy tensor of a system in the situation of [[post-sr-matter-isolation-and-total-stress-energy]]: $T$ is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$, satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ there (for the adopted models this is the conclusion of [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]; for any other system it is an explicit premise), and satisfies the zero side-flux condition $T^{ib}=0$ on the spatial faces for $i=1,2,3$. Put $Q^b(s):=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ and $P^b:=Q^b/c$. Then: (a) $Q^b(s)$ is finite for every $s\in[s_1,s_2]$ and $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$; (b) consequently $P^b$ is independent of $s\in[s_1,s_2]$; if $P$ is future timelike, its invariant mass $\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$ is independent of $s$ as well; (c) if the side flux does not vanish, the exact balance is the finite-flux identity of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]], and no conservation is asserted; (d) no transformation law for $P^b$ under a change of inertial chart or slicing is asserted: without an admissible-region flux argument, $P^b$ is a chart-component integral and is not claimed to be a four-vector; no noncompact, asymptotic or gravitational-energy statement is made, and the reading of $P^b$ as the system's four-momentum is the model's interpretation of the integral, not a measurement.
before.strategy: Clause (a) applies [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(c) to the box $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$ under the measured hypotheses (conservation and vanishing side flux); the invariance of the invariant mass in (b) is immediate because $P$ is a constant future timelike vector and $\eta(P,P)$ is then constant, using the invariant-mass formula of [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]. Clause (c) is the general balance case of the same theorem. Clause (d) records the exact scope: the theorem proves constancy of the chart integrals and nothing about their transformation under a change of chart, which would require the oriented hypersurface flux construction; no noncompact limit is taken. No empirical premise is used.
